family_title: Parameter sharing, random bases, spectral transforms and extreme-efficiency adapters

methods.name: VeRA
methods.paper_title: VeRA: Vector-based Random Matrix Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \Lambda_b\, B\, \Lambda_d\, A,\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen, random (seeded), shared by all adapted layers};\ \Lambda_b=\mathrm{diag}(b),\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}},\ \Lambda_d=\mathrm{diag}(d),\ d\in\mathbb{R}^{r}\ \text{trained per layer}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out} + r
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: W_q, W_v of RoBERTa/GPT-2/Llama/ViT); one shared random pair sized to the largest layer
methods.structure: frozen shared random bases with trainable diagonal scalings: \Delta W = \mathrm{diag}(b)\,B\,\mathrm{diag}(d)\,A factors through a fixed random r-dimensional space; only the row scaling of B and the rank-channel scaling are learned
methods.mergeable_reason: Lambda_b B Lambda_d A is a fixed-shape matrix that can be added to W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: b = 0 (so \Delta W = 0); d initialised to a constant (a tunable hyper-parameter; 0.1 in the GLUE runs and the HF default d_initial=0.1); A, B Kaiming-initialised and regenerable from an RNG seed, so in the paper only b, d and the seed need storing (HF PEFT nevertheless saves the projections by default, save_projection=True)
methods.key_idea: Freeze one pair of random low-rank matrices shared by every layer and learn only two scaling vectors per layer, so per-layer storage is a vector instead of a matrix; random features plus learned scalings suffice for adaptation.
methods.results_note: Matches LoRA on GLUE (RoBERTa) and E2E (GPT-2) and in Llama 7B/13B instruction tuning while using an order of magnitude or more fewer trainable parameters (theoretical count in its Table 1 for RoBERTa-base: 18.8K for VeRA vs 589.8K for LoRA at r=16; 18.4K is the r=1 VeRA figure).

methods.name: PVeRA
methods.paper_title: PVeRA: Probabilistic Vector-Based Random Matrix Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: h = W_0x + \alpha\,\Lambda_b B\, z,\quad z = \mu + \epsilon\odot\sigma,\ \epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I),\quad [\mu;\sigma] = \Lambda_d A x;\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{2r\times d_{in}},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{frozen random shared};\ d\in\mathbb{R}^{2r},\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\ \text{trained};\ \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{task}+\beta\sum \mathrm{KL}(\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)\,\|\,\mathcal{N}(0,I));\ \text{deterministic inference: } W = W_0 + \alpha\Lambda_b B\,\Lambda_{d_\mu}A_\mu
methods.trainable_params: d_{out} + 2r
methods.locus: linear layers (paper: W_q, W_v of ViT); shared random matrices as in VeRA
methods.structure: VeRA with a stochastic (VAE-style reparameterised) rank-r bottleneck: the r-dim code is sampled from a Gaussian whose mean and std are VeRA-style scaled random projections of x; KL prior on the code (HF PEFT reads the second half of \Lambda_d A x as a log-variance, \sigma = \exp(\tfrac12\log\sigma^2), and adds no explicit \alpha)
methods.mergeable_reason: With mean (deterministic) inference z = mu the update is a fixed matrix that merges like VeRA; Monte-Carlo sampling mode at test time is input-dependent and cannot be merged.
methods.identity_at_init: b = 0 (HF: \lambda_b zeros), d = d_{initial} (0.1); so the adapter output is zero at init
methods.key_idea: Make VeRA's shared-random-basis bottleneck probabilistic so the adapter learns a distribution over adaptations, enabling uncertainty estimates while keeping VeRA's tiny footprint and mergeability.
methods.results_note: Outperforms VeRA and the other benchmarked adapters (seven adapters in total in the comparison) on average on VTAB-1k with ViT backbones; deterministic (mean) inference keeps it mergeable.

relations.note: same frozen shared random A, B and trainable scaling vectors, plus a reparameterised Gaussian bottleneck

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2512.07703 (Fillioux, Dec 2025); WACV 2026 confirmed by arXiv journal-ref and IEEE DOI 10.1109/WACV61042.2026.00243; Eqs. for mu/sigma = xA (.) d, z = eps*sigma + mu, KL loss, merge with A_mu checked; HF pvera/layer.py (lambda_b zeros, lambda_d = 0.1, logvar chunking, mean at eval) checked.
corrections: structure: noted that the HF implementation parameterises the second half as a log-variance and has no alpha factor
results_note: abstract says 'seven adapters' were evaluated, not 'six other' adapters; reworded
code_url: added official code link from the abstract

methods.name: NOLA
methods.full_name: Compressing LoRA using Linear Combination of Random Basis
methods.paper_title: NOLA: Compressing LoRA using Linear Combination of Random Basis
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \Big(\sum_{j=1}^{l}\beta_j B_j\Big)\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{k}\alpha_i A_i\Big),\quad B_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen pseudo-random (generated from a seed, optionally shared across layers)};\ \alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{k},\ \beta\in\mathbb{R}^{l}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: k + l\ \ (\text{independent of } r,\ d_{in},\ d_{out})
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: attention projections of GPT-2, LLaMA-2, ViT)
methods.structure: LoRA factors constrained to the linear span of k (resp. l) frozen random basis matrices; \Delta W is bilinear in the two coefficient vectors and has rank \le r
methods.mergeable_reason: After training the two linear combinations are materialised, and their product BA is added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not specified in the paper. Official code (UCDvision/NOLA, gpt/examples/NLG/src/model_nola.py) zero-initialises both coefficient vectors, and each NOLA factor also carries a frozen offset matrix (LoRA-style reset: Kaiming for A, zero for B), so \Delta W = 0 at init with non-zero gradients for the B-side coefficients; with the paper's pure-span formula, zero-initialising both alpha and beta would give zero gradients. Bases are U(-1,1) from a stored seed and are regenerated on the fly in forward/backward to save memory
methods.key_idea: Decouple the parameter count from rank and width (LoRA's rank-1 floor) by expressing each LoRA factor as a learned mixture of seeded random basis matrices, PRANC-style; only the seed and the mixture coefficients (optionally 4-bit quantised) are stored.
methods.results_note: On LLaMA-2 70B NOLA is about 20x more compact than the most compressed (rank-1) LoRA without accuracy loss; also matches LoRA on GPT-2 E2E and ViT few-shot classification with fewer parameters.

relations.note: reparameterises LoRA's A and B

motivated by the low-intrinsic-dimension literature it cites (Li et al. 2018; Aghajanyan et al. 2021); a random linear subspace of the LoRA factor space rather than of the full parameter space; its direct ancestor is PRANC (see papers)
our observation: (alpha, beta) -> (A, B) is linear, i.e. theta_D = P theta_d with a block-diagonal dense random P

methods.name: RandLoRA
methods.full_name: RandLoRA: full-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning with random bases
methods.paper_title: RandLoRA: Full-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \sum_{j=1}^{n} B_j\,\Lambda_j\,A\,\Gamma_j,\quad B_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen random (A shared by all terms; bases shared across layers)};\ \Lambda_j\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r},\ \Gamma_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times d_{in}}\ \text{diagonal, trained};\ n=\min(d_{in},d_{out})/r\ \text{for a full-rank update (layer oriented so that } d_{in}=\min(d_{in},d_{out}))
methods.trainable_params: n\,(r + d_{in}) = \tfrac{d_{in}^2}{r} + d_{in}\quad (n = d_{in}/r,\ d_{in}=\min(d_{in},d_{out}))
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: ViT/CLIP vision and text encoders, LLMs such as Qwen2, Phi3, Llama3)
methods.structure: sum of n rank-r terms, each a frozen random basis pair with trainable diagonal scalings on both the bottleneck (Lambda_j) and the input columns (Gamma_j); the sum has full rank min(d_in, d_out) with probability one
methods.mergeable_reason: The sum of scaled random products is a dense matrix added to W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: \Lambda_j = 0, so \Delta W = 0 (HF PEFT: randlora_lambda = 0, randlora_gamma = 1/\max(n, \min(d_{in},d_{out})), i.e. typically 1/\min(d_{in},d_{out}); update scaled by randlora_alpha/r, default 640/32); bases Kaiming-uniform from a seed, shared across layers and sliced to each layer's size
methods.key_idea: Separate the effect of parameter count from the effect of rank: combine many VeRA-like random low-rank terms with learned diagonal scalings to obtain full-rank updates at LoRA-like parameter budgets; the number of trainable parameters is inversely proportional to the basis rank.
methods.results_note: Full-rank updates help across vision, language and especially vision-language (CLIP) tasks, where RandLoRA significantly reduces and sometimes closes the gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning.

relations.note: a sum of VeRA-like scaled random products (diagonal scalings on the bottleneck and input columns) instead of a single one

methods.name: Intrinsic SAID
methods.paper_title: Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \theta^{D}_{i} = \theta^{D}_{0,i} + \lambda_i\,\big(\theta^{d-m}M\big)_i,\quad M = H\,G\,\Pi\,H\,B\ \ (\text{Fastfood transform: Hadamard } H,\ \text{Gaussian diagonal } G,\ \text{permutation } \Pi,\ \pm1 \text{ diagonal } B;\ \text{frozen});\ \theta^{d-m}\in\mathbb{R}^{d-m},\ \lambda\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\ (\text{one scale per layer})\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: d\ \text{for the whole model, including the classification head in the paper's count (e.g. } d_{90}\approx 207 \text{ for RoBERTa-Large on MRPC)}
methods.locus: the entire flattened parameter vector of the model (all layers), with layer-wise scaling
methods.structure: random linear subspace of the full parameter space: \Delta\theta = \mathrm{diag}(\lambda)\,P\,\theta_d with a structured random (Fastfood) projection P
methods.mergeable_reason: The projected update is a fixed parameter offset that can be added to theta_0.
methods.identity_at_init: \theta^{d} = 0 recovers the pretrained parameters exactly
methods.key_idea: Fine-tuning works in a tiny random subspace: optimise a d-dimensional vector projected into the full parameter space; the small d needed (intrinsic dimension) explains why huge models fine-tune well on little data. SAID adds per-layer scales.
methods.results_note: Optimising about 200 parameters (d90 = 207 with SAID) projected into RoBERTa-Large's full space reaches 90% of full fine-tuning performance on MRPC (about 800 for QQP); larger and longer-pretrained models have lower intrinsic dimension.

relations.note: alternative low-dimensional fine-tuning: a random linear subspace of the full parameter space versus LoRA's structured low-rank factor space; LoRA cites this intrinsic-dimension finding as motivation

methods.name: Tied-LoRA
methods.full_name: Tied Low-Rank Adaptation (weight tying + selective training)
methods.paper_title: Tied-LoRA: Enhancing parameter efficiency of LoRA with Weight Tying
methods.formula_latex: W_\ell = W_{0,\ell} + \Lambda_{v_\ell}\, B\, \Lambda_{u_\ell}\, A,\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{tied (one copy shared by all layers)};\ \Lambda_{u_\ell}=\mathrm{diag}(u_\ell),\ u_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{r},\ \Lambda_{v_\ell}=\mathrm{diag}(v_\ell),\ v_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\ \text{per layer};\ \text{each of } A,B,u,v \text{ is selectively trained or frozen (configs TL1--TL6; TL6 trains all)}
methods.trainable_params: \text{TL6: } r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{once for all layers} + L\,(r + d_{out})\ \text{in total; per adapted matrix } \approx r + d_{out} + \tfrac{r(d_{in}+d_{out})}{L}
methods.locus: paper: the fused QKV projection (d x 3d) of every transformer layer; applicable to any linear layer
methods.structure: a single low-rank pair BA shared across depth, modulated per layer by diagonal scalings of its rows and rank channels; selective freezing yields a lattice of sub-configurations
methods.mergeable_reason: The low-rank path is linear, so each layer's Lambda_v B Lambda_u A can be merged into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Per Table 1: TL2/TL6 (VeRA-like): A, B \sim \mathcal{N}, u = 1, v = 0 (exact identity); TL3--TL5 (LoRA-like): A \sim \mathcal{N}, B = 0, u = v = 1 (exact identity); TL1 (only tied A trained): A, B \sim \mathcal{N}, u = v = 1, so \Delta W \neq 0 at init; \alpha = r, removing the \alpha/r scaling
methods.key_idea: Tie one LoRA pair across all layers and train only what is needed (shared factors and/or per-layer scaling vectors); a framework containing LoRA and VeRA as corners of the same design space.
methods.results_note: TL6 (trainable tied A, B plus per-layer u, v) stays within roughly 1-2% of LoRA across five tasks (on average 1.36% below LoRA with LLaMA-2 7B) and beats LoRA on IWSLT-2017 De-En translation with 12.5% of its parameters; on GSM8K it needs 4.3% of LoRA's parameters for a comparable score.

methods.name: ShareLoRA
methods.paper_title: ShareLoRA: Parameter Efficient and Robust Large Language Model Fine-tuning via Shared Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: \text{ShareA: } W_\ell = W_{0,\ell} + \alpha\, B_\ell\, A,\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{shared by all layers},\ B_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{per layer};\quad \text{ShareB: } \alpha\, B\, A_\ell;\quad \text{ShareAB: } \alpha\, B A\ \text{for every layer (all factors trained)}
methods.trainable_params: \text{ShareA: } r\,d_{out} + \tfrac{r\,d_{in}}{L}\ \text{per adapted matrix (i.e. } L r d_{out} + r d_{in} \text{ per module type)}
methods.locus: attention projections (ShareA_qkv: A_Q, A_K and A_V are each shared across all layers, one shared A per projection type) or all linear layers ('sharing all'), on RoBERTa, GPT-2 and LLaMA 1/2/3
methods.structure: LoRA in which one factor (the down-projection A, the up-projection B, or both) is a single matrix shared across depth; \Delta W_\ell = B_\ell A spans a common row space for all layers
methods.mergeable_reason: Each layer's B_l A is an ordinary low-rank matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Inherits LoRA initialisation (up-projection zero, so Delta W = 0); not discussed separately in the paper
methods.key_idea: Share LoRA's down- (or up-) projection across all layers: the shared subspace removes redundancy, roughly halves parameters or more, and acts as a regulariser that improves robustness and continual-learning transfer.
methods.results_note: 44%-96% fewer trainable parameters than LoRA with maintained performance on RoBERTa, GPT-2 and LLaMA 1/2/3, and up to 1.2% higher average accuracy in zero/few-shot and continual fine-tuning settings.

methods.name: PRoLoRA
methods.paper_title: PRoLoRA: Partial Rotation Empowers More Parameter-Efficient LoRA
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + BA,\quad B = \big[\,B_u\ \big|\ \big(B_0;\,\mathrm{Roll}(B_0,s_B);\dots;\mathrm{Roll}(B_0,(n{-}1)s_B)\big)\big],\quad A = \Big[\,A_u;\ \big(A_0\,|\,\mathrm{Roll}(A_0,s_A)\,|\cdots|\,\mathrm{Roll}(A_0,(m{-}1)s_A)\big)\Big];\ A_u\in\mathbb{R}^{u\times d_{in}},\ B_u\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times u}\ \text{(unshared ranks)},\ A_0\in\mathbb{R}^{(r-u)\times d_{in}/m},\ B_0\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}/n\times(r-u)}\ \text{trained};\ \mathrm{Roll} = \text{cyclic shift along the rank dimension}
methods.trainable_params: u\,(d_{in}+d_{out}) + (r-u)\Big(\tfrac{d_{in}}{m} + \tfrac{d_{out}}{n}\Big)
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: all linear layers of LLaMA-2 / Tulu instruction tuning)
methods.structure: intra-layer sharing: each LoRA factor is a broadcast of one small chunk along the hidden dimension, the copies differentiated by rank-dimension cyclic permutations, plus u unshared ranks; \Delta W is block-structured with blocks related by rank permutations
methods.mergeable_reason: The expanded B and A are ordinary matrices, so BA merges into W_0 exactly as in LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (whole matrix); A_u Kaiming-uniform and the shared chunk A_0 with a rectified Kaiming bound computed from the full hidden size d_in so both parts have equal scale
methods.key_idea: Reuse parameters inside a layer: broadcast one chunk of each LoRA factor across the hidden dimension (more rank per parameter) and break the resulting repetition with cheap rotations and a few unshared ranks; a strict superset of LoRA.
methods.results_note: With half the trainable parameters of LoRA, PRoLoRA still outperforms LoRA on multiple instruction-tuning benchmarks and scales to larger LLMs.

methods.name: MoS
methods.paper_title: MoS: Unleashing Parameter Efficiency of Low-Rank Adaptation with Mixture of Shards
methods.formula_latex: W_\ell = W_{0,\ell} + B_\ell A_\ell,\quad B_\ell = \mathrm{Route}^{c}\big([B^{pub}, B^{pri}],\, I^{b}_\ell\big),\quad A_\ell = \mathrm{Route}^{r}\big([A^{pub}, A^{pri}],\, I^{a}_\ell\big);\ \text{each rank vector of } A_\ell, B_\ell \text{ is the concatenation of } l \text{ shards retrieved from global pools by fixed random index matrices } I_\ell;\ \text{pools trained, indices frozen; private shards are used by one layer only}
methods.trainable_params: \approx e\,(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix on average (global pools of size } eL(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per linear-layer type), while each layer uses rank } r > e
methods.locus: all linear-layer types of LLaMA-2/3 (one global pool per layer type)
methods.structure: global inter- and intra-layer sharing: LoRA factor vectors are assembled from shards of shared public/private pools via subset selection, pair dissociation (separate pools for A and B), vector sharding and shard privatisation; routing is index-based and input-independent
methods.mergeable_reason: Indices are fixed, so after training each layer's B_l A_l is a fixed low-rank matrix that merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: public and private B pools zero-initialised (\Delta W = 0); A pools with PRoLoRA-style rectified Kaiming bounds; index matrices sampled once at random
methods.key_idea: Pure sharing across layers hurts because all layers get the same update; cheap differentiation strategies (random subsets, dissociated A/B pools, shards, private shards) restore diversity while keeping the high sharing ratio.
methods.results_note: About 8x parameter savings relative to standard LoRA at matched performance on instruction-tuning benchmarks (MMLU, BBH, GSM8K, etc.), with ablations confirming each differentiation component.

methods.name: VB-LoRA
methods.paper_title: VB-LoRA: Extreme Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning with Vector Banks
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + BA,\quad \text{every length-}b\text{ sub-vector } u \text{ of every column of } B \text{ and row of } A:\ u = \sum_{s=1}^{h} w_s(\sigma)\,\alpha_s,\ \ w(\sigma) = \mathrm{Softmax}\big(\mathrm{TopK}(\sigma,k)\big);\ \text{bank } \{\alpha_s\in\mathbb{R}^{b}\}_{s=1}^{h}\ \text{shared by all modules and layers (trained)},\ \sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{h}\ \text{logits per sub-vector (trained)}
methods.trainable_params: \text{training: } \tfrac{r(d_{in}+d_{out})}{b}\,h\ \text{logits per matrix} + hb\ \text{shared};\ \ \text{stored } (k=2,\ \text{uint8 indices}): \tfrac{3}{2}\,\tfrac{r(d_{in}+d_{out})}{b}\ \text{per matrix} + hb\ \text{shared}
methods.locus: any linear layer, sharing across modules and layers (paper: query/value or all linear layers of RoBERTa, GPT-2, Llama2, Mistral, Gemma)
methods.structure: divide-and-share: LoRA's rank-one component vectors are split into sub-vectors, each a sparse top-k convex combination (simplex-constrained) of a globally shared vector bank -- a hierarchical, constrained CP/tensor factorisation spanning the whole model
methods.mergeable_reason: After training the logits are discarded, the selected mixtures define fixed B, A, and BA merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not exact: bank \sim U(-0.02, 0.02) and logits \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.1^2) (HF defaults), so \Delta W is small but non-zero; an all-zero bank is avoided because it would give zero gradients
methods.key_idea: Treat all LoRA parameters of a model as sub-vectors drawn from one small learned vector bank via differentiable sparse top-k admixture, so storage stops scaling with model width, depth and number of modules.
methods.results_note: On Llama2-13B instruction tuning VB-LoRA uses only 0.4% of LoRA's stored parameters yet scores higher on MT-Bench; competitive with or better than VeRA, Tied-LoRA and LoRA on GLUE, E2E (about 20% fewer stored parameters than VeRA) and GSM8K/MATH (Mistral-7B, Gemma-7B).

papers.title: Measuring the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes
papers.claim: Training in a random low-dimensional subspace theta = theta_0 + P theta_d reveals an intrinsic dimension at which solutions first appear; it is often far smaller than the parameter count and nearly constant across model sizes for a given task.

papers.title: Asymmetry in Low-Rank Adapters of Foundation Models
papers.claim: In BA adapters, A extracts features and B maps them to outputs; tuning B is inherently more effective, a random untrained A performs nearly as well as a tuned one, and training only B tightens an information-theoretic generalisation bound.

papers.title: PRANC: Pseudo RAndom Networks for Compacting deep models
papers.claim: A deep model can be reparameterised as a linear combination of several frozen, randomly initialised basis networks, so it can be stored as one seed plus mixture coefficients, compressing classifiers about 100x.

notes: Scope: 28 methods in five sub-clusters. (1) Frozen random bases with learned coefficients or scalings: VeRA, PVeRA, NOLA, RandLoRA, Intrinsic SAID. (2) Cross-layer or intra-layer sharing and tying: Tied-LoRA, ShareLoRA, PRoLoRA, MoS, VB-LoRA, Uni-LoRA, Lily, RaSA, FacT, MoSA, MiSS. (3) Tiny trainable cores inside frozen weight-derived or random bases: LoRA-XS, LoRA-SB, TinyLoRA, LaMDA, LoRA-Mini, SVFT, FRoD. (4) Transform-domain sparse updates: FourierFT, WaveFT, SSH, LoCA, C3A. Unifying observation: almost every method here is Delta W = Phi(P theta) with frozen P (random, SVD-derived, DFT/DCT/DHT/DWT, index or tiling maps) and a small trainable theta; Uni-LoRA states this projection view explicitly for LoRA-space variants. Uncertainties: (a) Identity at init is not exact for VB-LoRA, Uni-LoRA, LoRA-XS (sigma=1e-5), SVFT (official code), FourierFT (paper default), SSH (Kaiming), C3A (HF default xavier), LoRA-Mini (Kaiming on all matrices) and LoRA-SB (starts at an approximate first full-FT step by design). (b) The NOLA paper does not specify coefficient initialisation; the official code zero-initialises both coefficient vectors and adds a frozen offset per factor (see entry). (c) MoSA (ICLR 2026): no arXiv id found; lambda = 0 in the official code. (d) Lily trainable-parameter count is approximate (router placement varies). (e) FRoD: the paper states that only Sigma_i and the sparse S_i are trainable (confirmed in verification). (f) Several statements marked 'our observation' are derived algebraically rather than claimed by the authors (MiSS = LoRA with frozen block-summing A; LoRA-XS as a special case of SVFT; NOLA in the Uni-LoRA template). (g) LaMDA and LoRA-XS formulas are converted from the papers' row-vector convention; the trainable core then sits next to Sigma_r, an equivalent reparameterisation. Venues checked: MiSS is ICLR 2026 (proceedings PDF checked); LoRA-XS is ECAI 2025; LaMDA is EMNLP 2024 Findings; C3A is ACL 2025 Findings; Lily is ACL 2025 Findings; SSH is NAACL 2025; PRoLoRA is ACL 2024; Tied-LoRA is NAACL 2024. A web-search summary claimed ShareLoRA and LoRA-SB were at ICLR 2026; the ICLR 2026 proceedings list (5,351 titles) contains neither, so ShareLoRA is recorded as arXiv and LoRA-SB as an ICLR 2025 SCOPE workshop paper (its ICLR 2026 submission was withdrawn). WaveFT, TinyLoRA, ShareLoRA and LoRA-Mini have no confirmed venue. HF PEFT (v0.21.1, 2026-09-29) implements VeRA, PVeRA, VB-LoRA, Uni-LoRA, RandLoRA, FourierFT, WaveFT, C3A, MiSS (Bone was removed in favour of MiSS), Lily, TinyLoRA and FRoD. Overlaps with other family files: svft (multiplicative), fact/c3a/miss (shape), lora-sb (init-rank), and the hf-peft list. Considered but excluded as low-uptake or better placed elsewhere: ASLoRA (arXiv 2412.10135), E2LoRA (ICLR 2026, entropy-guided adaptive cross-layer sharing), EigenLoRAx (CVPRW 2025, principal subspaces recycled from trained adapters), MASA (arXiv 2510.06005), LoTR/LoRETTA/Compacter/HyperFormer (tensor/adapter families), SHiRA (selective), ETHER/RoAd (multiplicative), HydraLoRA (composition).
